visual_action: A static, medium shot of Barack Obama sitting in a chair in a well-lit room with a couch and a side table. He speaks directly to the camera, gesturing with his hands.

cast.name: Barack Obama
cast.evidence: He is the sole person on screen, speaking directly to the camera for the entire duration of the video.

cast.name: Kamala Harris
cast.evidence: The on-screen text says "Vote for Kamala Harris" and Barack Obama says, "Vote for Kamala Harris."

cast.name: Tim Walz
cast.evidence: The on-screen text says "Vote for... Tim Walz" and Barack Obama says to vote for him.

on_screen_text.text: Barack Obama: Vote for Kamala Harris and Tim Walz

spoken_summary: Barack Obama urges viewers to vote, stating that the election will be close and could be decided by a handful of votes in each precinct. He encourages people to talk to their family and friends, make a plan, and go to the polls. He explicitly endorses Kamala Harris and Tim Walz and directs viewers to the website iwillvote.com to find their polling place.
audio_music: The audio consists solely of Barack Obama's speech. There is no background music or sound effects.
editing_pacing: The video is a single, static talking-head shot. The only editing effect is the sequential appearance of large, yellow text at the bottom of the screen, emphasizing key words from the speech.
central_claim: Because the election will be extremely close, every single person must vote for Kamala Harris and Tim Walz.
intended_effect: To create a sense of urgency and persuade viewers to vote for the Democratic candidates, Kamala Harris and Tim Walz.
